title: Sentry Student / Free
description: Claim Sentry through GitHub Education when eligible, keep on-demand billing disabled, create a generic project, and stop before exposing any DSN or auth token in public walkthrough data.

steps.title: Open GitHub Student Pack
steps.body: Open the GitHub Student Developer Pack and locate Sentry. Confirm the current student entitlement and quotas on the provider page before relying on them.
steps.humanGate: GitHub login, student verification, OAuth, CAPTCHA/MFA, terms, or any billing decision require your confirmation. Do not enable paid on-demand usage.

steps.title: Find Sentry
steps.body: Use the page search or CTRL Find on page to locate Sentry, then open the Sentry student offer.

steps.title: Redeem or sign in
steps.body: Redeem the student entitlement or sign into an existing Sentry account. If the student offer is not granted, stop before purchasing anything; the regular free path can be evaluated separately.
steps.humanGate: Account creation, OAuth consent, email verification, MFA and terms acceptance are user-controlled.

steps.title: Confirm zero-cost guard
steps.body: Confirm the account shows the student entitlement or another explicitly $0 plan and that on-demand billing is disabled. Do not add a payment method for this setup.
steps.humanGate: If Sentry requests payment or enabling on-demand usage, stop and return to your project operator.

steps.title: Create a project
steps.body: Create a Sentry project for the application you are monitoring. Choose the platform that matches the application, such as JavaScript/browser for a public website or React Native for a native mobile app. Use a generic project name in any public walkthrough; project-specific naming belongs in private state or a local handoff.

steps.title: Stop at SDK setup
steps.body: When Sentry shows the SDK installation/setup page, stop and return to your project operator. Do not paste DSNs, auth tokens, private repository paths, account identifiers, private hostnames, or project-specific configuration into a public walkthrough, issue, screenshot, or public repository file.
